title: Impact on COE Prices Exerted by Car Rental Companies that Lease Out Private Hire Cars
what_it_is: Impact on COE Prices Exerted by Car Rental Companies that Lease Out Private Hire Cars

sections.label: COE bids by private hire cars
sections.summary: Minister says there is no evidence private hire car companies raised COE bid prices, and LTA has monitored stable demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether there is any evidence to suggest that car rental companies, particularly those leasing to the private hire vehicles (PHVs) market, have affected Certificate of Entitlement (COE) bid prices in the past year; (b) if not, whether a study on this will be conducted; and (c) whether such rental cars and those used for PHVs can be removed from the COE bidding process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: There is no evidence that private hire car (PHC) companies have caused the increase in COE bid prices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA has been monitoring the market closely and, over the past year, the demand for COEs from PHC companies as well as the overall PHC population have been stable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Recognising the role which shared point-to-point (P2P) transport plays in our land transport system, from 2012, taxi operators did not have to bid for a COE to register their taxis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Instead, they draw from the pool of Category E (Open) COEs and pay the Category A COE prevailing quota premium.

sections.label: Removing PHCs from COE bidding
sections.summary: Removing PHCs from the bidding pool and creating a new category would be difficult to enforce and raise compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Removing PHCs from the bidding pool and creating a new category with specific requirements, such as a minimum number of trips to prevent abuse, would be difficult to enforce and add to the compliance cost for PHC operators, drivers and, ultimately, consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA will continue to monitor the P2P sector and study schemes for further enhancement.

sections.label: PHC and taxi numbers
sections.summary: The point-to-point sector has about 70,000 PHCs versus close to 14,000 taxis, about five times more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If you look at the point-to-point transportation sector today, the number of PHCs are about 70,000 versus about close to 14,000 taxis – about five times more.

sections.label: PHC population and COE demand
sections.summary: The PHC population and COE demand are stable, and PHC entities have not submitted higher bids or reserved prices than non-PHC entities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The population of PHCs is stable and the demand for COEs has also remained stable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And, in fact, the PHC entities have actually not submitted bids or reserved prices which are higher than non-PHC entities.
